france24fr.description: La présidente par intérim Delcy Rodriguez a défendu samedi l'accord "historique" signé entre Washington et Caracas, assurant face aux doutes que le Venezuela conserverait sa souveraineté sur les champs pétroliers amenés à être exploités par les Etats-Unis.

france24fr.title: Suisse : Fusillade lors d'un festival techno, 1 mort et 5 blessés
france24fr.description: La police suisse est mobilisée dimanche pour tenter de retrouver le ou les auteurs des tirs qui ont fait un mort et cinq blessés dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche en marge d'une rave party à Aarau, dans le nord de la Suisse près de Zurich. Selon la presse locale, les coups de feu ont été tirés avant 03h00 (01h00 GMT) en marge de la "Aarauer Rave", fête techno annuelle qui a rassemblé quelque 3 500 personnes à l'hippodrome d'Aarau entre samedi après-midi et dimanche matin.

france24fr.description: Un bateau avec à son bord plus de 250 passagers a coulé, dimanche, au large de la République turque de Chypre du Nord autoproclamée. Une opération de recherche et de sauvetage est en cours. france24fr.description: Depuis son retour au pouvoir, Donald Trump a fait du départ des personnes en situation irrégulière du territoire américain une priorité. Mais lorsque leur expulsion vers leur pays d’origine s’avère difficile, voire politiquement sensible, les autorités américaines se tournent de plus en plus vers une alternative : leur expédition vers des États tiers, dont le Cameroun.

france24fr.title: Crue dans l'Himalaya : les opérations de secours progressent péniblement
france24fr.description: Les opérations de secours progressent pas à pas dimanche au Népal et en Chine, dans des conditions périlleuses, pour tenter de retrouver des survivants quatre jours après la crue dévastatrice qui a fait plus de 750 morts et causé des dégâts considérables. Plus de 3 000 personnes restent encore portées disparues dans cette région isolée de l'Himalaya, mais l'espoir d'extraire des rescapés de la mer de boue et de débris qui a enseveli ses villages s'amenuise au fil des heures.

phys-org.title: Centuries of child labor left lasting spinal damage in Dutch children, study finds
phys-org.description: Children in the postmedieval Dutch workforce worked so hard that their spines became worn and deformed, with some children affected before they even had a chance to lose their baby teeth, a new study published in the International Journal of Paleopathology finds.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump
proj-syn.description: Rather than keeping their heads down as US President Donald Trump wages another trade war with Canada, European leaders must recognize that they could be next. Like Canada, the European Union is a middle power whose future prosperity and security will depend on solidarity with economic peers.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.
